The Artisans Behind the Sound of Korea! The Amazing Process of Making Traditional Instruments

Hello, this is King Process.

Traditional Korean drums, moktak, daegeum, and janggu are all made by skilled artisans, but each produces sound in a different way. They adjust the tension of animal hide, hollow out wood, and make precise holes in bamboo. In this video, we follow the making of four traditional Korean instruments.

First is drum making by artisan Im Dong-guk. He learned bukmeugi, the craft of making traditional drums, from his father Im Seon-bin, a recognized holder of the tradition. He makes the wooden drum body, prepares the hide, and stretches it tightly to bring out the drum’s sound. We also see how he checks the sound at the end of the process.
